data.narrative:
Lambda, a Series E AI & Software company that has raised $3.15B to date, operates within a competitive frontier-tech sector represented by 1 public comparable (Palantir) and 8 private peers including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition.

The valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method: stage-progression analysis. Using total capital raised ($3.1B) as a proxy for baseline value and applying a 1.4x step-up multiplier typical for Series E advancement, this method implies a valuation of $4.4B. A peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient narrow-set comparables—while 12 same-sector peers exist, none satisfied minimum thresholds for direct stage, valuation tier, or adjacent-stage matching. Constructing a range around the stage-progression result yields low and high estimates of $3.7B and $5.1B respectively, anchored to the $4.4B median.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $3.7B to $5.1B, centered at $4.4B. Key uncertainties include the reliability of capital raised as a valuation proxy absent disclosed financials, the applicability of standard step-up multiples to frontier-stage AI infrastructure, and material gaps in comparable data. Resolution of these uncertainties would require disclosure of revenue run-rate, unit economics, or forward guidance to strengthen the triangulation.
